conventions.convention: PEC uses H₀(curl), defined as the H(curl) graph-norm closure of compactly supported smooth real vector fields. The continuous gauge removes the entire curl kernel K; the discrete gauge removes K_h.
Permittivity ε and permeability μ are positive homogeneous scalar constants. Weighted and ordinary L² kernel orthogonality therefore coincide.

The spectral theorem assumes AC, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice; a nonempty bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedral cavity with connected boundary; shape-regular matching affine tetrahedral meshes with maximum diameter tending to zero; and the three PE09 supplier statements for that exact setting.
Canonical edge moments are applied only to smooth inputs. The smooth approximation lemma asserts eventual PEC membership and convergence for each fixed compactly supported smooth field.
Spectral convergence counts full eigenvalue multiplicities and uses symmetric L² subspace gap; it does not select convergent individual eigenvectors within repeated eigenspaces.

load_bearing.statement: On a bounded connected Lipschitz domain, V=H₀(curl;Ω), K={u∈V:curl u=0}, and X=V∩K⊥ε. For positive constant ε,μ, the positive PEC eigenproblem is μ⁻¹(curl u,curl v)=λ(u,v)ε for every v∈X. On a matching affine tetrahedral mesh, V_h=N_h¹∩V, K_h=ker(curl|V_h), and X_h=V_h∩K_h⊥ε; the discrete problem replaces X by X_h.

Assume Countable Choice. On a real Hilbert space, compact self-adjoint nonnegative operators T,T_n that converge strongly, are uniformly bounded, and are sequentially collectively compact have no spurious positive eigenvalue limits. Every isolated positive eigenvalue of T is approximated with exactly its multiplicity in an isolating interval whose closure avoids other spectral points, and the cluster subspaces converge in symmetric Hilbert-space gap.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. On a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron with connected boundary, every graph-bounded sequence in the full-kernel gauge X has a strongly L²-convergent subsequence, and there is CΩ such that ‖u‖₂≤CΩ‖curl u‖₂ for every u∈X.

Assume Countable Choice. On a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedron with a shape-regular matching affine tetrahedral mesh family of maximum diameter tending to zero, for every u∈X and every mesh sequence h_n→0 there are u_h_n∈X_h_n converging to u in H(curl).
Assume Countable Choice. If Ω is bounded open, u_n∈H₀(curl;Ω), u_n→u strongly in L², and the curls are bounded in L², then a subsequence of the curls converges weakly to curl u and u∈H₀(curl;Ω).

Under the stated AC/CC/DC, contractible connected-boundary Lipschitz polyhedral cavity, positive constant scalar coefficient, refining shape-regular tetrahedral mesh and exact PE09 supplier hypotheses, the continuous PEC problem has isolated positive eigenvalues of finite multiplicity. Each isolated positive eigenvalue is approximated with full multiplicity and symmetric L² eigenspace-gap convergence. Every finite limit of positive discrete eigenvalues is a continuous eigenvalue.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier definitions and the regular-decomposition, commuting-projection and discrete-compactness interfaces against their Maxwell uses. The consumer preserves real graph-closure spaces, lowest-order oriented Whitney elements, shape-regular matching affine meshes and choice/topology hypotheses. Its full-kernel discrete gauge lies within the supplier's gradient-orthogonal space. Kernel approximation uses the separate homogeneous projection family and its curl commutation, rather than assuming boundary preservation for the full family. The supplier page distinguishes those families and does not import Maxwell spectral conclusions in reverse.
